issues.title: Prove a spectrum theorem relating confined eigenvalues to curvature and torsion
issues.body:
## Problem

The exact effective-mass statement is spectral: `m_n = (ħ/c) sqrt(lambda_n)`. For constant-curvature circular confinement, this reduces to the familiar curvature relation, but the general replacement of `sqrt(lambda_n)` by an averaged `sqrt(kappa^2 + tau^2)` requires an additional theorem or controlled approximation.

## Goal

Establish rigorous bounds or asymptotics for confined eigenvalues in terms of curvature, torsion, topology, boundary conditions, and admissible WCT geometry.

## Required work

- Define the admissible class of confinement geometries and operators.
- Prove lower/upper bounds for `lambda_n` using curvature/torsion invariants.
- Identify conditions under which the curvature-average mass law is exact, asymptotic, or only approximate.
- Quantify corrections away from constant-curvature locked loops.
- Test the theorem numerically on nontrivial geometries.

## Completion criteria

- [ ] A precise theorem statement is written with hypotheses.
- [ ] Bounds/asymptotics connect `lambda_n` to geometric invariants.
- [ ] Equality cases are characterized.
- [ ] Numerical examples verify the predicted scaling and correction terms.
- [ ] The status of the general curvature-average mass law is updated accordingly.

Source: `DERIVATION_CLOSURE.md`, Remaining work item 2.

issues.title: Prove stability or construct a ghost-free higher-derivative completion
issues.body:
## Problem

The corrected curvature action is generically fourth order in derivatives, including time derivatives when the covariant `Box psi` term is retained. The current derivation does not yet establish absence of Ostrogradsky-type extra modes, positivity of the Lorentzian Hamiltonian, or spectral/orbital stability of localized solutions.

## Goal

Demonstrate that the physical WCT sector is dynamically acceptable, or replace the higher-derivative formulation with a mathematically equivalent degenerate/auxiliary-field completion that removes pathological branches.

## Required work

- Derive the canonical structure of the corrected higher-derivative action.
- Identify all propagating branches and constraints.
- Determine whether the Hessian is degenerate in the required sense.
- Analyze Hamiltonian boundedness in the physical sector.
- If needed, construct an auxiliary-field or constrained completion.
- Test linear and nonlinear stability around relevant vacua and localized states.

## Completion criteria

- [ ] Propagating degrees of freedom are counted explicitly.
- [ ] Ghost/extra-mode conditions are derived.
- [ ] A bounded physical Hamiltonian or equivalent constrained formulation is demonstrated.
- [ ] Linear dispersion is stable in the intended parameter region.
- [ ] At least one localized solution passes spectral/orbital stability tests.
- [ ] The stable parameter domain is documented reproducibly.

Sources: `DERIVATION_CLOSURE.md`, Remaining work item 6; `WCT_CORRECTED_VARIATIONAL_CLOSURE_DRAFT.md`, canonical-status limitations.

issues.title: Resolve the canonical finite-k selection mechanism in the corrected variational action
issues.body:
## Problem

The corrected real curvature action has no linear fourth-order contribution about the zero vacuum because the nonlinear weight satisfies `F(u) = O(u)` near `u = 0`. Therefore it does not by itself produce the claimed Swift–Hohenberg-type finite-band dispersion around the zero vacuum.

The current draft identifies three distinct possibilities: finite-k selection around a nonzero background, a separate effective Swift–Hohenberg rail, or a revised higher-derivative weight with `G(0) > 0`. These are not equivalent and the canonical theory must choose or derive one.

## Goal

Determine which mechanism actually generates finite-k selection in the corrected WCT formulation and derive its dispersion relation from first principles.

## Required work

- Choose a constant nonzero background `psi0 = A0 exp(-i omega0 t)` and expand `psi = psi0 + eta`.
- Derive the full quadratic action in `eta` and `eta*`.
- Derive the exact Fourier-space dispersion matrix.
- Determine whether a real finite unstable band exists while satisfying `gamma^2 < 4 kappa theta`.
- Compare the resulting band with the effective Swift–Hohenberg rail.
- If the nonzero-background route fails, explicitly evaluate the `G(0) > 0` alternative and/or retain the rail as an independent effective model.
- Update the canonical equation set so the repository no longer presents non-equivalent mechanisms as interchangeable.

## Completion criteria

- [ ] Quadratic perturbation theory around the selected background is derived explicitly.
- [ ] The dispersion eigenvalues are obtained analytically or symbolically.
- [ ] Finite-k instability conditions are stated as inequalities in model parameters.
- [ ] The preferred canonical mechanism is selected and justified.
- [ ] The relationship to the Swift–Hohenberg rail is classified as derived, asymptotic, phenomenological, or rejected.
- [ ] Documentation and source-of-truth equations are updated consistently.

Source: `WCT_CORRECTED_VARIATIONAL_CLOSURE_DRAFT.md`, sections 6, 8, and 9.

issues.title: [P0] Close the dilation-obstruction question for the positive scalar WCT functional
issues.body:
## Goal
Turn the currently documented fixed-norm dilation obstruction into a reproducible analytic/numerical closure result for the positive scalar WCT energy used by `vacuum.py`.

## Why this matters
If the declared free-space functional cannot possess an energetically self-bound finite-radius minimizer under fixed norm, that result constrains the entire eigen pipeline more strongly than additional solver tuning. Conversely, any stationary localized state must be shown not to be a finite-box or saddle artifact hidden by the scaling direction.

## Scope
- Derive the fixed-norm dilation/scaling behavior of each energy term for an explicit normalized family.
- Numerically evaluate the energy along increasing dilation scales and verify the asymptotic trend.
- Compare the dilation direction against the constrained Hessian when a stationary candidate exists.
- State clearly whether the analysis rules out a stable free-space minimizer for the current positive scalar functional, only rules out a global minimizer, or remains inconclusive.
- Do not introduce new confining terms or retune coefficients in this issue.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The scaling derivation is documented in-repo with assumptions and dimensional conventions.
- [ ] A deterministic numerical dilation experiment reproduces the predicted trend.
- [ ] The result is connected explicitly to the stationary-state/Hessian gate.
- [ ] The repository records one of: `DILATION_OBSTRUCTION_CONFIRMED`, `DILATION_OBSTRUCTION_NOT_DECISIVE`, or a comparably precise frozen classification.
- [ ] If the obstruction is decisive, the README explains that failure to find a self-bound state is an expected structural result rather than a solver failure.

issues.title: [P1] Extend stability validation beyond the real-scalar sector
issues.body:
## Goal
Determine whether a real-scalar Hessian pass is sufficient for the canonical WCT field, and if not, add the missing phase/complex-sector stability analysis.

## Current gap
The current pipeline explicitly validates the exact **real-sector** constrained second variation of the scalar WCT energy. If the canonical physical field is complex or carries additional perturbation sectors, a nonnegative real-sector Hessian does not by itself establish full linear stability.

## Scope
- State explicitly whether the canonical field for this repository is real-only or complex-valued.
- If complex-valued, derive the second variation for independent amplitude and phase/imaginary perturbations, including any coupling terms.
- Identify gauge/phase zero modes and separate them from physical instabilities.
- Extend the stability artifact to record which perturbation sectors were audited.
- Prevent the validator from labeling a state fully stable when required sectors are unevaluated.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The field-content assumption is documented unambiguously.
- [ ] Required perturbation sectors are derived and implemented, or a mathematical argument shows the real sector is complete for the declared model.
- [ ] Expected zero modes are identified and treated separately from negative modes.
- [ ] Tests cover at least one stable and one unstable synthetic sector.
- [ ] `WCT_CONFINED_STATE_V1` or its successor records stability-sector completeness.

**Status: OPEN — priority 4; difficulty 5/5.** The exact-rational block-enclosure checker and adversarial finite-matrix fixtures PASS. They do **not** establish a sharp enclosure for the frozen production real L² target `T=P exp(100 A_140) P`, where `P` removes **only** phase and x/y translations. The numerical result `1.3690254532021537` is not globally certified; the retained production bound is `[0,1.6494305049768293e22]`.

issues.title: D4: certify an explicit quantitative nonlinear orbital perturbation basin
issues.body:
## Objective

Turn the validated **qualitative local all-time orbital H² stability** result from #25 into a fully explicit, reproducible initial-data stability radius for the **same frozen periodic model and nearby exact continuum root** established in #24. This is a quantitative follow-up, **not** a reopening of either completed theorem or a substitute for #21–#23.

## Existing certified inputs (2026-10-15)

- [PR #26 at e9a2b589](https://github.com/rickyjreyes/wct-pde/pull/26) validates a smooth nearby real-D4 root on the length-42 **two-dimensional** torus (D4 is square symmetry, not four spatial dimensions).
- The [independent theorem appendix](https://github.com/rickyjreyes/wct-pde/blob/e9a2b589243cfc8fa1492b67a02949c9ba660e93/docs/D4_INDEPENDENT_CLOSURE_APPENDIX.tex) proves qualitative local all-time orbital stability for sufficiently small arbitrary complex H² perturbations, including mass-changing and symmetry-breaking data.
- On the **exact modulated symmetry slice**, it gives a radius `rho=1e-8` and `W(phi+z)-W(phi) >= 0.00082085097379 ||z||_(H²,m)^2`. This is a **slice energy inequality only**, **not** an arbitrary-data orbital basin.
- The existing independent root/coercivity checks share the FLINT/Arb arithmetic backend and strategy. They are not external peer review or proof-assistant verification.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pin exact root/certificate receipt, binary input parameters, domain, H² mean/physical norm normalization, phase/translation orbit and conserved functional; do not silently transfer a discrete or whole-space bound.
- [ ] Derive **quantitative phase/translation modulation** with explicit invertibility/conditioning and a certified neighborhood for arbitrary initial data, including mass-normal and non-D4 perturbations. Bound the relation between orbital distance and exact-slice H² size.
- [ ] Produce outward and reproducible upper Taylor/energy constants relating the initial orbital distance to `|W(u0)-W(phi)|`; combine with the existing lower slice estimate and first-exit argument.
- [ ] State and certify a numerical pair `(epsilon_*, delta_*)` (or a nontrivial explicit function `delta(epsilon)` on a specified range), with `delta_*>0`, such that `dist_H²(u0,O_phi)<delta_*` implies `sup_(t in R) dist_H²(u(t),O_phi)<epsilon_*`. Explicitly handle both time directions via the already proved global H² continuation.
- [ ] Independently replay every new quantitative constant with outward arithmetic and deterministic/adversarial fixtures, including near-singular modulation Gram data and mass-changing/symmetry-breaking inputs; preserve exact source, receipt hashes, scripts and CI checks.
- [ ] Publish a checkable theorem and numeric constants, or retain an exact **OPEN/BLOCKED** obstruction without converting `rho=1e-8` or qualitative `forall epsilon exists delta` into an unsupported numeric basin.

## Boundaries and relationship to existing issues

#24 and #25 **remain CLOSED** for their original scoped criteria. A quantitative orbital basin is optional strengthening, not an unfulfilled premise of the published qualitative theorem. This issue does **not** certify attraction, large-data/global orbital stability, an L²-only basin, finite-grid quotient-gain optimality, whole-space confinement, four-spatial-dimensional lifetime/persistence, or all of comprehensive D4 closure.

**Priority:** P2 (after #21; may run in parallel with #22). **Difficulty:** 3/5.

Evidence: [comprehensive report](https://github.com/rickyjreyes/wct-pde/blob/e9a2b589243cfc8fa1492b67a02949c9ba660e93/docs/D4_COMPREHENSIVE_CLOSURE_REPORT.md) · [independent stability audit](https://github.com/rickyjreyes/wct-pde/blob/e9a2b589243cfc8fa1492b67a02949c9ba660e93/docs/D4_INDEPENDENT_STABILITY_AUDIT.md) · [passing independent CI](https://github.com/rickyjreyes/wct-pde/actions/runs/38775402440).
